artifacts.notes:
26 pages, PDF 1.4, produced by Corel PDF Engine with a creation date of
2013-06-28. Contents: Part One, ICEL publication policies (nature and purpose of
ICEL, approval of texts, permissions, copyright, royalties, contracts,
variations, rubrics, sense lines, ICET/ELLC texts); Part Two, the schedule of
royalties; Part Three, the copyright acknowledgment; and an appendix carrying a
specimen ICEL contract and, last, the Global Computer Networks clause.
The text layer extracts cleanly with hyphenation across line breaks preserved as
printed; small caps extract with an intervening space ("C OMMITTEE"), so the
layer is a finding aid and not an exact transcription source.
artifacts.rights_basis:
The booklet is ICEL's own corporate policy document and carries no reuse grant
over itself. The Global Computer Networks clause it prints at artifact page 26
reaches "ICEL texts and translations that have been approved by the Conferences
of Bishops, have received the recognition of the Holy See, and have subsequently
been promulgated for use" — approved liturgical translations, which this booklet
is not. So the clause that makes ICEL's liturgical English publishable here says
nothing about redistributing these particular bytes, and the exact remote bytes
are identified and hashed while no payload is retained. This is a disposition of
the file, not of the text the file authorises: the rights record at
src/sources/inventories/icel-web-permission-rights-v1.toml settles the text.

edition.notes:
This is the fuller booklet that the Commission's summary page links and that the
sibling edition web-2026-08-01 recorded as not retrieved. It is retrieved now.
Its appendix, printed page 25, carries the clause Use of ICEL Materials on
Global Computer Networks, which is the express permission this project's
publication of ICEL text stands on; guidance/liturgical-text-publication-policy.md
section 3.1 quotes it and could not previously cite it from a repository record.

Two internal facts a later reader needs. First, printed page numbers run two
behind PDF page numbers through the body and one behind in the appendix: the
grant is printed page 25 and artifact page 26, and the acknowledgment rules are
printed pages 18-19 and artifact pages 19-20. Every passage record here states
the artifact page, which is what the bytes support. Second, the booklet
throughout gives the Commission's corporate title as "International Committee on
English in the Liturgy, Inc." — the older form. ICEL's own current files, its web
copyright page, and the 2010 Roman Missal notice all read "International
Commission on English in the Liturgy Corporation". Condition (2) of the grant
points to the web page for the appropriate acknowledgment, so the current wording
governs and the booklet's older corporate title must not be copied into a notice.
edition.publication: The Commission's own booklet of publication policies, published as a 26-page PDF at https://www.icelweb.org/PubPolicy.PDF. The title page reads EFFECTIVE DECEMBER 1995 / Amended 2008, 2010, 2013; the file's own document metadata gives a creation date of 28 June 2013.

passages.context:
The whole clause, read on 2026-08-21 from the retained bytes, artifact page 26,
printed page 25, under the heading "Use of ICEL Materials on Global Computer
Networks". It is the last item of the appendix and the last page of the booklet.

"ICEL texts and translations that have been approved by the Conferences of
Bishops, have received the recognition of the Holy See, and have subsequently
been promulgated for use on the date established by the Conferences of Bishops
may be reproduced in a non-commercial site ("Site") on the global computer
network commonly known as the Internet without obtaining written or oral
permission, subject to the following conditions:

(1) there must be no fee charged to access the Site or any of the ICEL
translations, texts, or music, thereon;

(2) The appropriate ICEL copyright acknowledgment must appear on the first and
last pages and/or frames within the Site displaying the ICEL translation or text
(see www.icelweb.org and click on "copyright policies");

(3) The ICEL translations and texts must be followed exactly;

(4) These policies do not grant a license to publish texts in any other form or
any other right in ICEL's name and marks, and the Site may not display the ICEL
translations or texts or otherwise use the ICEL name in any way that implies
affiliation with, or sponsorship or endorsement by, ICEL;

(5) ICEL reserves the right to terminate or modify its permission to use its
translations and texts;

(6) ICEL reserves the right to take action against any party that fails to
conform to these policies, infringes any of its intellectual property rights, or
otherwise violates applicable law."

Four facts are established per text before the clause reaches it, and they are
facts about that text and never inferences from the book it is printed in: that
it is ICEL's own, approved by the Conferences of Bishops, recognised by the Holy
See, and promulgated for use. A provisional, Green Book or Gray Book text is
outside the clause by its own terms.

Condition (2) points away from this booklet for the wording of the
acknowledgment. Take that wording from ICEL's current copyright page and from
the notice ICEL itself prints on the file the text was read out of, not from the
Part Three examples at artifact pages 19-20, which give the Commission's older
corporate title.
passages.notes: The clause the summary page at icelweb.org/copyright.htm does not carry. A reader who checks that page and stops concludes no web permission exists; the sibling passage permissions-and-royalties on edition web-2026-08-01 is that reading, made when this booklet had not been retrieved, and should be read beside this one rather than instead of it.

passages.context:
Part One, "ICET/ELLC Texts", read on 2026-08-21 from the retained bytes, artifact
pages 11-12, printed pages 10-11. Registered because this repository already
publishes nine of these texts, on the English Language Liturgical Consultation's
own grant, and here the position is corroborated by the other party.

The booklet lists the texts: the Lord's Prayer, Apostles' Creed, Nicene Creed,
Kyrie, Gloria in Excelsis, Sursum Corda, Sanctus/Benedictus, Agnus Dei, Gloria
Patri, Benedictus (Canticle of Zechariah), Te Deum, Magnificat (Canticle of
Mary), Nunc Dimittis (Canticle of Simeon). Then:

"The texts, whether in their original form (1975) or as revised by ELLC (1988),
are in the public domain and as such do not require permission for reproduction.
It is sufficient to acknowledge the source of the text, for example: English
translation of the [insert title] by the International Consultation on English
Texts or the English Language Liturgical Consultation."

ICEL adds a format request that is not a rights condition: "ICET/ELLC texts
employ not only sense lines but also special indentations, all of which were
worked out after extensive discussion and agreement by the representatives of the
various church bodies. ICEL cannot be a party to any violation of the integral
texts agreed to in good faith by the participants in ICET/ELLC. Except in the
case of musical setting of the ICET/ELLC texts, ICEL strongly recommends that the
special format of the texts prepared by the participants in ICET/ELLC be
followed."

Two limits, both of which this repository already observes. These are the
ecumenical common texts and nothing else: not one is a proper, and no oration is
within reach of them. And an ELLC text is not the approved English of the Roman
Rite — ELLC reads "And also with you" where the 2011 Missal reads "And with your
spirit" — so an ELLC text must never be served as a Roman Missal text.
passages.notes: Corroborates [the_ellc_grant] in src/sources/inventories/liturgical-english-rights-v1.toml from a second and independent party. That entry rests on ELLC's own permissions page; this is the ICEL side saying the same thing, and it is stronger than a grant because it is a statement that no grant is needed.

passages.context:
Part One, the sections "ICEL Copyright", "Royalties" and "Contracts", read on
2026-08-21 from the retained bytes, artifact pages 5-6, printed pages 4-5.
Registered so that the licensing route and the standing web permission are held
apart, because conflating them is exactly how this repository previously reached
the wrong answer.

Why ICEL claims copyright at all: "ICEL copyrights its texts in order to maintain
under the civil law and international conventions the Church's ownership of these
texts used by Catholics in their worship. The legal safeguard provided by
copyrighting the texts helps to preserve their literary and liturgical integrity
under the ecclesiastical authority given to the conferences of bishops by the
Second Vatican Council and by subsequent instructions of the Apostolic See."

The royalty regime and its one stated free class: "a royalty fee is charged to
all publishers. ICEL does not charge for the reproduction of its texts when they
appear in materials produced by individual parishes, schools, religious houses,
and the like for their private and non-commercial, nonprofit use. Even in such
cases, however, the requisite acknowledgment and copyright notice should always
appear."

The contract route: "Except as noted elsewhere, a form of agreement must be
executed between ICEL and each licensee. A new contract must be executed for each
new text used". The information a request must supply is enumerated over the
following page — exact title, purpose, retail price, print run, the complete list
of ICEL texts by element, the complete list of non-ICEL material.

HOW THIS RELATES TO THE WEB GRANT, stated because the two are easy to run
together. The free class named here is about materials a parish or school
produces, and it does not describe a permanently published website; the previous
reading of ICEL's summary page turned on exactly that and concluded that a
licence was the only route. The Global Computer Networks clause at artifact page
26 is a separate provision with its own six conditions, it applies "without
obtaining written or oral permission", and it is the provision this project
stands on. The words "Except as noted elsewhere" opening the Contracts section
are the booklet's own acknowledgment that the contract route is not the whole of
it. No contract is executed, no licence issues, and no royalty arises, because
the clause dispenses with the request rather than granting it.
passages.notes: Also relevant to the permission-versus-authentication sequence the USCCB's 2025 guidelines describe, in which ICEL issues a licence after Secretariat authentication: that sequence is the contract route on these pages, and it is never entered when the internet clause applies, because no licence issues at all.

passages.context:
Part One, "Sense Lines", read on 2026-08-21 from the retained bytes, artifact
page 11, printed page 10. Condition (3) of the Global Computer Networks clause
says the translations "must be followed exactly"; this page is what ICEL means
by it in the one respect a corpus schema can get wrong silently.

"One important element of style and format is the arrangement in sense lines
(sometimes called sight lines) of those liturgical texts which by their nature
are acclamatory or proclamatory: the prayers and most noninstructional
materials. ... Sense lines are used in the liturgical books issued by the
Apostolic See, in most vernacular liturgical books, and in publications for
popular use.

Such sense lines must be respected in the reproduction of texts — as well as in
paragraphing, division into stanzas, and the like. If only a few lines of a given
liturgical text are quoted in commentaries and the like, the division into sense
lines may be indicated, as is done with quoted verses, by the use of a virgule or
solidus (/)."

The specimen contract in the same booklet states the same requirement as a
contractual term at artifact page 21, clause 2(a): the publisher "shall adhere
strictly to the TEXT ... and specifically must follow the wording, spacing, sense
lines, capitalization, and punctuation of such printed text, with the sole
exception that spelling may vary (e.g., honor/honour) to accommodate the usage in
a particular country." That is a licence term and not this project's instrument,
but it shows what the rightsholder counts as exactness, and the spelling
exception is the one variance ICEL itself contemplates — which is also why an
England-and-Wales copy and a United States copy of the same universal text may
legitimately differ in spelling without either being wrong.

The operative consequence for this repository: a schema that cannot carry line
structure cannot store an ICEL oration and satisfy condition (3). Line structure
is not presentation here; it is part of what must be followed exactly.
passages.notes: The USCCB's 2025 publication guidelines carry the same demand in their own words — excerpts verbatim including capitalization and punctuation, with the poetic structure of texts provided in sense lines generally preserved — so the requirement holds from two directions and is recorded here from the rightsholder's own.

passages.context:
Part Three, "The Copyright Acknowledgment", read on 2026-08-21 from the retained
bytes, artifact pages 19-20, printed pages 18-19. This is the content behind
condition (2) of the Global Computer Networks clause, and it is what an
attribution mechanism generated from metadata has to be able to produce.

The booklet opens by saying that "the required form of acknowledgment of ICEL
materials in a specific work will always be given in the contract or letter of
permission sent by ICEL", which is the licensing route and not this project's;
what remains generally applicable is the list of elements and the specimen
forms.

"ELEMENTS OF ACKNOWLEDGMENT. The acknowledgment of ICEL materials should always
include: 1. name of the ICEL copyrighted work being reproduced, printed in
italics or underlined; 2. the symbol (c), or the word "Copyright," or the
abbreviation "Copr."; 3. the year of original publication of the copyrighted
work; 4. ICEL's corporate title in full as below: International Committee on
English in the Liturgy, Inc. (In successive references within a single
acknowledgment, the references after the first may be abbreviated: ICEL.) 5. The
phrase "All rights reserved" at the end of the acknowledgment."

Under ACKNOWLEDGMENT OF AN ENTIRE WORK the specimen is "The English translation
of the Rite of Marriage (c) 1969, International Committee on English in the
Liturgy, Inc. All rights reserved." Where several sources are quoted, "the
primary source should be named first" and the remaining ICEL texts follow "in
chronological order".

Under ACKNOWLEDGMENT OF EXCERPTS: "In acknowledging excerpts of ICEL texts it is
preferable to name the element(s) or the specific rite(s) being reproduced",
with two specimens of the form "The English translation of the [named elements]
from [Work] (c) [year], International Committee on English in the Liturgy, Inc.
All rights reserved."

THE CORPORATE TITLE HERE IS THE OLDER ONE AND MUST NOT BE COPIED. This booklet
says "International Committee on English in the Liturgy, Inc." throughout.
ICEL's current copyright page, and the notice ICEL itself prints at the foot of
every page of its own free Missal chant files, both read "International
Commission on English in the Liturgy Corporation". Condition (2) sends the
reader to the web page for the appropriate acknowledgment, so the current form
governs. The element list above is what survives from this page: name the work,
carry the symbol, carry the year of original publication, give the corporate
title in full, end with "All rights reserved" — and, for an excerpt, name what
was excerpted.
passages.notes: Element 3, the year of original publication, is why one acknowledgment cannot be generated for the whole corpus: the Roman Missal English is 2010, the Lectionary for Mass 1969/1981/1997, Eucharistic Prayers for Masses with Children 1975. The year travels with the text, from metadata.

work.author: International Commission on English in the Liturgy Corporation
work.description: The Commission's own public statement of who may reproduce its liturgical translations, on what terms, and with what acknowledgement. Registered because this repository's decision not to carry the approved English of the postconciliar Roman Missal rests on a rights position, and a rights position stated only in this project's prose is an assertion; stated against the rightsholder's own published terms it is evidence. ICEL is a mixed commission of eleven Catholic bishops' conferences, established at Rome in 1963 and erected as a mixed commission under Liturgiam authenticam on 15 September 2003; it is not a publisher and licenses its texts to publishers authorised by the conferences.
